ai_summary:
Great Britain's wind output currently reaches 3.6 GW, with estimated Scottish wind output delivering 2.4 GW, which corresponds to 23.8% of installed Scottish wind capacity. Reflecting this substantial renewable generation, Scottish carbon intensity stands at 0 gCO2/kWh, in stark contrast to the GB-wide average of 206 gCO2/kWh. However, transmission bottlenecks between Scotland and southern demand centres continue to necessitate system rebalancing. Scottish generation curtailed so far today stands at 914 MWh, resulting in a constraint cost of about £49,792. To compensate for this displaced clean energy, thermal generation elsewhere on the network was ramped up, requiring an estimated 173,565 m3 of gas burned elsewhere to replace it and emitting an additional 320 tonnes CO2. 

Extrapolating these constraint costs across the year indicates an estimated total yearly cost of curtailment of £18 million. Distributed across annual national electricity demand, this volume of grid constraint expenditure adds an estimated £0.06/MWh to everybody's invoice in the UK, highlighting the ongoing financial and environmental costs of cross-border transmission limitations.
